chunks: As for the hadith which Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام:
"The maximum of what menstruation may be is eight, and the minimum of what it may be is three."

This hadith is anomalous; the group has unanimously agreed to abandon acting upon it. Even if it were sound, its meaning would be that when a woman’s habit is not to menstruate for more than eight days, then she has istiḥāḍah and the blood continues with her such that the blood of menstruation cannot be distinguished for her from the blood of istiḥāḍah, then the maximum she counts from the days of menstruation is eight days, according to what her habit had been before the continuation of the blood. We shall explain what indicates this interpretation later, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.

key_terms.التَّأْوِيلِ: interpretation, the reconciliatory meaning given to the report
key_terms.الْحَيْضُ: menstruation, the menstrual bleeding under discussion in legal rulings
key_terms.الْعِصَابَةُ: the scholarly body or the Shia community of transmitters/jurists who agreed on leaving this report
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةٌ: three, the stated minimum duration in the cited report
key_terms.ثَمَانٍ: eight, the stated upper limit in the cited report
key_terms.شَاذٌّ: anomalous, referring to a report not accepted for legal practice
key_terms.عَادَتُهَا: her established habit, used here as the basis for determining the counted days

ai.seo_question: How is the hadith about menstruation lasting up to eight days understood in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This passage cites a hadith from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام stating that menstruation may last up to eight days and no less than three. It then notes that this report is considered anomalous and not acted upon, and explains that, if accepted, it would be interpreted specifically in the case of a woman with an established habit whose bleeding continues indistinguishably as istiḥāḍah.
